rechecked_since_hcza.make_row_corrections_fix: Effect on other funds: the lookup first tries (cik, quarter, phrase, field items, reason), then field items, then field names. Only the HPS hook writes the new keys, so other funds fall back to the old key unchanged (the diff adds only 61 HPS lines). Two weaknesses. (1) The key still holds content, not context: two specs with the same fields, values and reason on different contexts still collide. The fix works here only because each reason quotes its context. Keying on spec_context(spec), or carrying the context in the SPECS tuple, would be robust. (2) tuple(sorted(fields.items())) raises TypeError on any spec whose field value is a list or dict. That fails loudly, not silently, and only for CIKs being regenerated.
rechecked_since_hcza.shadowed_correction_lines: Loader (_apply_row_corrections): row_corrections.csv then by_context are concatenated in file order and applied in that order per key, so the last line wins. Today the wrong lines are shadowed: 31 (First Lien c-195) by 32, 33 (c-253) by 34, 35 (c-314) by 36, 30 (Unsecured on c-389, reason cites c-393) by 39 (same value). The effective output is correct, and corrected_fields dedups. But this is order-dependent: any sort, dedupe or first-wins change to the file or loader would silently publish First Lien on three Second Lien loans. The audit log also records the wrong values as 'applied'. The lines are uncommitted, so removing lines 30, 31, 33, 35 does not touch committed history, and the effective output is the same. Remove them before commit.
